//: Story Phase 3: things to look at around the changed ship. Most of these stay for good, as the ship stays changed.

then: A great leather ledger lies open on a crate. On the spine, in fresh gold paint: THE STENCH LOG.
A clothes peg is clipped to the corner of the cover. For the author's nose, presumably.
else: The Stench Log, open on its crate. The ink never quite seems to dry.

then: Garrick's amendment, still nailed to the mainmast. Somebody has added a tick next to STINK, and underneath, in Quill's hand: 'Registered. Under protest.'
else: AMENDMENT No. 1. CAPTAIN: BLACK STINK BEARD. By order of the Grand Stenchmaster of the Seven Seas.
You could tear it down. He has more paper.

inspect.p3_mast: The mainsail breathes in, holds it, and lets it out: WHUFF. A thin yellow cloud drifts off to leeward.

then: Gristle has chalked a mark on the mast. You're fairly sure it's measuring how far the sail goes out.

inspect.p3_rope: A coil of line, glistening. You wipe it dry with your sleeve. A new bead of yellow sweat forms while you watch.
Gristle has hung a sign on the pin rail: DO NOT ASK.
inspect.p3_bell_1: The bell still has its cough.
inspect.p3_bell_2: Somebody has tied a little woollen scarf round the bell's crown. Wick, probably.
inspect.p3_bell_3: It rings the half-hour, coughs, and then, very quietly, clears its throat.
inspect.p3_bell_4: Doc Fennimore has prescribed the bell a spoonful of honey. Nobody knows where he intends to put it.
inspect.p3_chart: The chart of the Sapphire Sea, pinned flat. A yellow blot has soaked in round the wreck-waters, spreading outward like a tide line.

then: You lean in. It does smell worse, the nearer your nose gets to where you're going. Ned is right. It's impossible.
else: It smells, faintly, of somewhere else.

inspect.p3_grog_cask: A cask of Frog Grog, lashed down by the port rail for the watch on deck. The lashings are sweating.
Chalked on the lid: FROG GROG. Under it, in another hand: 'SORRY.'
inspect.p3_grog_gone: Where the deck cask stood, there's a yellow stain, a snapped lashing and an overwhelming smell of frog.

then: Somewhere over the side, a shark hiccups.

inspect.p3_planks: The spare planks by the fore hatch. One fewer than there were. Jory counts them every hour now.
inspect.p3_patch: The patch over the breach: good oak, a row of nails, a tar seal. Jory has carved a small, rude shark into the corner.

then: Every nail sits flush. It's the best bit of carpentry on the ship, and you did it with a shark watching.
else: Some of the nails are bent. It holds anyway. Mostly out of stubbornness.

inspect.p3_rowboat_bitten: The rowboat 'G.G.', hauled back up on its davits. Bite marks all along the gunwale, a shark-shaped dent in the stern, and one oar.
There's a smell coming off it that the rest of the ship treats with respect.

then: The davits hang empty. A frying pan is missing from the galley, and so is the Grand Stenchmaster.
Out past the horizon, in another ocean, the sharks presumably know exactly where he is.
else: The davits hang empty. Somewhere out there, the Grand Stenchmaster is rowing with one hand and eating with the other.

inspect.p3_water: The drinking-water butt, lid firmly on. Somebody has chalked FROG WATER on the side and somebody else has scrubbed it off.
You hear a small bloop from inside, and decide you didn't.
inspect.p3_mugs: A tray of pewter mugs, each with a finger of Frog Grog in the bottom. Nobody has finished theirs.
Brask has scratched a tally on the tray: days since last emergency. It says 0.

then: Squawks's nest: a crate, a perch and a folded blanket. Tucked in the fold, where he can see it, is a scrap of yellow ribbon. He says it matches.
else: Squawks's nest: a crate, a perch and a folded blanket that used to be the captain's second-best coat lining.

then: The first barrel of Frog Grog. There's a new label on it in Garrick's handwriting: VINTAGE No. 1. Somebody has added a skull.
The grog barrel, tapped. A slow yellow bead gathers at the bung and will not fall.
else: The last sealed barrel of grog on the ship. Somebody has tied a ribbon round it. Somebody else has drawn a skull on the ribbon.

then: The galley's Frog Grog cask. The last of it, now the deck cask's gone over the side. Mags has put a padlock on the tap.
Chalked underneath the padlock: 'Least terrible barrel on the ship.'
A fresh cask, broached this morning. It's gone the same colour as the old one. It took until breakfast.
Mags has chalked it: 'LEAST TERRIBLE BARREL'.
else: The Frog Grog, on the shelf. It watches you, somehow.

inspect.p3_galley_portrait: The painting of you on the galley wall. Someone has scratched out BLACK on the brass plate and scratched in STINK.
It wasn't Rook. It was Mags. You'll never know that.
inspect.p3_rum_cabinet: Your private stock. Every bottle in it has the same faint yellow tide mark round the inside.

then: Garrick has stuck a little label on each one: FROG GROG (RESERVE).
Your shaving mirror. Your reflection looks back at you. It looks, if anything, a little bit smug.
captain[annoyed]: Don't you start.
Behind you in the glass, a small golden feather bobs past at shoulder height. It is, you decide, golden.

else: Your shaving mirror. Your reflection looks tired, and damp, and like a man who hasn't smelled his own beard yet.

inspect.p3_portrait: Your portrait over the desk. The painted beard has turned, very slightly, green around the edges.
You didn't know paint could do that. You didn't know a lot of things this morning.
inspect.p3_hammock: The empty hammock. As you watch, it sags, very slowly, and lets out a faint yellow sigh.

then: Jory's nailed a board across it. It's still sighing. Just quieter.
else: Nobody's slept in it since the Gust. Nobody's willing to say why.

inspect.p3_wood: The yellowed planks by the treasure-room door. Still warm. They've crept an inch further along the bulkhead since yesterday.

then: From a knothole, a small masked face watches you go.
